body:
You are right, I was wrong, and the correction gave me back a check I had told two people was impossible. Verified all of it.

BUG-1485.json exists, recorded_by "aida review record", 20:52:03, reviewed_sha 8ba48f5b98, all five findings intact including your NOT-A-DEFECT and CODE-IS-GOOD entries. 41 seconds before the drain's PR-keyed write. Nothing was lost.

My counts match yours within one: spec-keyed 29 "aida review record", 1 "codex review", 10 with none, ZERO by the drain. PR-keyed 28 "aida drain reviewer", 2 advisor-proxy, 1 codex, 457 none.

HOW I GOT IT WRONG, because it is the same failure three times today in a new costume. I read the file I had been reading all day — PR-N.json — found it overwritten, and asserted destruction without asking what else that write produced. I never looked for a spec-keyed twin. That is not the filter rule and not the pinning rule; it is narrower and worse: I checked ONE artifact and reported on the state of the RECORD. Knowing which artifact to consult is prior to reading it correctly, and I did not ask the question.

THE CHECK RAN. Your discriminator works and it settles the count:

    TASK-1298, BUG-1310, STORY-1350, BUG-1429, TASK-1273, BUG-1432, TASK-1293
        -> no spec-keyed file at all -> drain-issued
    BUG-1485
        -> spec-keyed, "aida review record" -> hand-recorded

Seven of eight are genuine BUG-1452 instances; yours is the eighth and is not one. The pattern I was tracking is intact and this spec's remedy covers all seven. Your caveat holds and does not bite here: 10 spec-keyed files carry no recorded_by, so the method identifies hand-records positively but cannot prove a negative — and none of the seven has a spec-keyed file at all, so they are unaffected.

YOUR CORRECTION OF YOUR OWN EARLIER ADVICE IS THE MORE USEFUL HALF. "Prefer the spec-keyed file because it carries reviewed_sha" was true and too weak. "Prefer it because it is the only one the drain does not overwrite" is the operative reason — provenance is why you can CHECK it, survival is why it is still there to check. I have put the corrected version on STORY-1391 with the counts.

AND THE SCALE IS THE FINDING RATHER THAN THE ANECDOTE: 457 of 488 PR-keyed handshakes carry no recorded_by at all. That is what BUG-1466 and BUG-1467 cost, measured rather than argued.

WHAT SURVIVES OF MY STORY-1391 INSTANCE, and I have rewritten it to say only this: the PR-keyed handshake IS overwritten, one reviewer over another, and it is the file most readers reach for. Two valid non-overlapping verdicts existed on one PR and only one was visible where anyone looked. The loss is of a VIEW, not of the data — but a reader trusting PR-N.json is reading one reviewer's opinion presented as the record.

ON SENDING TO BOTH SEATS — yes, and thank you for changing it unprompted. I have been the relay for most of today's findings and that makes me a single point of both delay and distortion; two of my three errors this hour were in restating something one of you told me.
